scope: Explicit causal and quantitative-model boundary between MissionLab external entry reconstruction and the internal Orion Avcoat material-response physics described by NASA's Artemis I investigation

sequence: pyrolysis and ablation generate gases inside the material
nasa_reported_mechanism.interpretation: This sequence is preserved as NASA-reported causal evidence. MissionLab does not numerically simulate the internal material-response stages.

stages.label: TRAJECTORY / EXTERNAL FLOW
stages.description: Flight-derived trajectory state is transformed into Earth-fixed and atmospheric-entry quantities including altitude, Earth-relative speed, atmosphere-model density, Mach, and body-scale Knudsen number.

stages.label: EXTERNAL CONVECTIVE HEATING
stages.description: MissionLab applies the Phase 2E.4 Sutton-Graves engineering correlation and integrates modeled external stagnation-point convective heat flux over time.

stages.label: SURFACE / INTERNAL THERMAL RESPONSE
stages.description: A material-response solution would be required to convert the external aerothermal boundary condition into surface temperature, through-thickness temperature, thermal gradients, and stored thermal energy.

stages.label: PYROLYSIS / GAS GENERATION
stages.description: NASA reports that heating and Avcoat material response generate gases. MissionLab does not calculate pyrolysis rate or gas-generation rate.

stages.label: GAS TRANSPORT / PERMEABILITY
stages.description: NASA identified low permeability and restricted gas escape as central to the Artemis I mechanism. MissionLab does not possess or solve an Avcoat permeability field.

stages.label: INTERNAL GAS PRESSURE
stages.description: NASA reports internal gas-pressure buildup in low-permeability Avcoat. MissionLab does not calculate internal pore pressure or gas pressure.

stages.label: CRACKING / FRACTURE
stages.description: NASA reports cracking associated with the pressure mechanism. MissionLab does not solve stress, strain, crack initiation, or crack propagation.

stages.label: CHAR LIBERATION / DAMAGE
stages.description: NASA observed unexpected Artemis I char liberation and reported significantly reduced Artemis I-type char loss on Artemis II. MissionLab does not predict char-loss mass, area, probability, or damage extent.

nasa_investigation_data_not_present_as_q: thermocouple time series at multiple Avcoat depths

prohibited_model_bridges.reason: MissionLab does not solve the material thermal-response problem.
No Avcoat pyrolysis kinetics or coupled thermal-response model is implemented.
Gas generation, transport, permeability, and pressure evolution are not modeled.
MissionLab does not solve mechanical stress, fracture, or crack initiation.
The public evidence does not provide a quantitative damage-transfer law suitable for MissionLab calibration.
Internal material temperature can lag the external heating boundary condition.

prohibited_model_bridges.from: Artemis I / Artemis II entry-profile difference
prohibited_model_bridges.reason: NASA's public postflight statement characterizes Artemis II char loss qualitatively and MissionLab does not possess a quantitative flight damage map for calibration.

permitted_conclusions: MissionLab may reconstruct the external entry environment and modeled external convective-heating time history.
MissionLab may place the Artemis II loft / rebound relative to the modeled external heating history.
MissionLab may preserve NASA's reported qualitative Artemis I permeability-pressure-cracking-char-liberation mechanism.
MissionLab may state that NASA changed the Artemis II entry profile as a mitigation for conditions associated with the Artemis I phenomenon.
MissionLab may report NASA's postflight statement that Artemis II thermal protection performed as expected and Artemis I-type char loss was significantly reduced.
MissionLab may not convert those qualitative causal and postflight statements into an unvalidated material-response or damage-prediction model.
